masteryZone.q: Which of the following describes the core legislative change introduced under 1. Separation of Executive & Legislative Functions?

The reduction of the Governor-General's Council to three members
The establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta
The introduction of the system of dyarchy
masteryZone.sol: The Charter Act of 1853 separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council and created a new 12-member Indian Legislative Council.

masteryZone.q: Suppose a young Indian subject wishes to compete for the elite covenanted civil service in 1855. Under the rules established by 3. Indefinite Charter Renewal & Local Representation, analyze the eligibility and selection procedure.
masteryZone.sol: The Indian subject is fully eligible. The Charter Act of 1853 threw covenanted civil services open to Indians via open competitive examinations. The candidate had to travel to London to sit for the competitive exams, as governed by the Macaulay Committee guidelines.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'local representation' introduced under 3. Indefinite Charter Renewal & Local Representation.
masteryZone.sol: Local representation meant that provincial governments (Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Agra) were given direct representation in the central law-making body (Legislative Council) by appointing British civil servants from their regions to act as legislative councillors.
